module.name: System.Threading
module.short: Task-based parallel programming library: thread pools, tasks, futures, continuations, cancellation and parallel loops

descr.p: System.Threading implements a Delphi-compatible Parallel Programming Library for Free Pascal. Instead of managing operating-system threads (TThread) directly, an application expresses concurrency as lightweight tasks (, ), typed asynchronous results (), non-blocking continuations (, ), cooperative cancellation () and data-parallel loops ().
Work items run on a work-stealing thread pool (). Unhandled exceptions raised by tasks are captured and re-raised in the waiting thread inside a flattened .
Anonymous procedures are used throughout the API, so programs using it need {$modeswitch functionreferences} and {$modeswitch anonymousfunctions}, and cthreads as the first unit on Unix.

element.short: Reference to a parameterless procedure; the body type of tasks and of

element.short: Method called by for each inner exception; set aHandled to True to mark it handled

element.name: TExceptionHandlerProc

element.name: EAggregateException
element.short: Exception that carries one or more exceptions raised by tasks or parallel loop iterations

descr.p: EAggregateException collects the exceptions raised by tasks (, , ) or by parallel loop iterations (, ). Nested aggregate exceptions are flattened into a single list.
Iterate over the inner exceptions with for E in Agg do (which yields exactly Count elements), index them with InnerExceptions, or let Handle filter out the ones the program can deal with.
The aggregate exception owns its inner exceptions and frees them when it is destroyed.

element.name: EAggregateException.TExceptionEnumerator
element.short: Enumerator returned by for for..in loops

element.name: EAggregateException.TExceptionEnumerator.Create
element.short: Creates an enumerator over a copy of the given exception array

element.name: EAggregateException.TExceptionEnumerator.MoveNext
element.short: Advances to the next inner exception; returns False after the last one

element.name: EAggregateException.TExceptionEnumerator.Current
element.short: The inner exception at the current position

element.name: EAggregateException.MaxLoggedExceptions
element.short: Maximum number of inner exceptions included in the text returned by ToString

element.name: EAggregateException.Create
element.short: Creates an aggregate exception containing the given exceptions, with the default or the given message

descr.p: The new object takes ownership of the exceptions in aExceptionArray.

element.name: EAggregateException.Count
element.short: Number of inner exceptions

element.name: EAggregateException.InnerExceptions
element.short: Indexed access (0..Count - 1) to the inner exceptions; the default property

element.name: EAggregateException.GetEnumerator
element.short: Returns an enumerator over the 0..Count - 1 inner exceptions

element.name: EAggregateException.Handle
element.short: Calls a handler for each inner exception and re-raises the ones that were not handled

descr.p: The handler is called once for every inner exception. If it leaves aHandled as False for at least one of them, Handle raises a new EAggregateException with the same message that contains only the unhandled exceptions; the handled ones stay owned by the original object. If all exceptions are handled, Handle returns normally.

element.name: EAggregateException.Add
element.short: Appends an exception to the list; the aggregate exception takes ownership of it

element.name: EAggregateException.ToString
element.short: Returns the message followed by the number of inner exceptions and the first MaxLoggedExceptions of them

element.name: TThreadPool
element.short: Work-stealing thread pool that executes tasks, futures and parallel loops

descr.p: TThreadPool manages a set of reusable worker threads and a monitor thread. Each worker has a local work-stealing queue next to the global queue; an idle worker takes work from other workers' queues before it goes to sleep. The monitor thread adds workers when queued work waits and CPU usage is low, and idle workers retire after a timeout.
Every method that schedules work accepts an optional pool; when it is omitted, is used. Create a separate pool to isolate a workload or to limit its number of threads.

All worker threads and the monitor thread are owned by the pool (FreeOnTerminate = False). Pool.Free terminates, joins (WaitFor) and frees all of them, so after it returns no pool thread is still running user code, destructors or the RTL thread epilogue.

element.name: TThreadPool.IControlFlag
element.short: Shared flag that lets only the first of several queued work items execute

descr.p: A control flag starts at -1. Each work item increments it just before running and executes only if the result is 0, so of all work items queued with the same flag only the first one to start runs; the others are skipped. Incrementing the flag before any item starts cancels all of them. Obtain a flag with .

element.name: TThreadPool.TProcThread
element.short: Procedure reference that receives a pool thread; the type of and

element.name: TThreadPool.Create
element.short: Creates a pool; worker threads are started on demand when work is queued

descr.p: The initial limits are MinWorkerThreads = max(2, ProcessorCount div 4) and MaxWorkerThreads = 2 * ProcessorCount.

element.name: TThreadPool.Destroy
element.short: Shuts the pool down and joins and frees all worker threads and the monitor thread

descr.p: Work items that are still queued are not executed. Because Destroy waits for every pool thread, it must not be called from a pool thread, and must not wait for the thread that calls Destroy (for example through TThread.Synchronize when the pool is freed from the main thread).

element.name: TThreadPool.NewControlFlag
element.short: Returns a new in its initial state

element.name: TThreadPool.QueueWorkItem
element.short: Queues a procedure or a TNotifyEvent for execution on the pool

descr.p: This is the low-level entry point used by tasks. It returns immediately and gives no way to wait for the item or to receive its exceptions; use for that. Work items queued with the same aControlFlag follow the rules described in .

element.name: TThreadPool.SetMaxWorkerThreads
element.short: Sets the maximum number of worker threads; returns False and changes nothing if the value is not greater than MinWorkerThreads

descr.p: The default minimum is max(2, ProcessorCount div 4), so on a machine with 16 or more logical processors SetMaxWorkerThreads(4) fails. To limit a pool to a small number of threads, lower the minimum first:

element.name: TThreadPool.SetMinWorkerThreads
element.short: Sets the minimum number of worker threads kept by the pool; returns False and changes nothing unless 0 <= aValue < MaxWorkerThreads

element.name: TThreadPool.MaxWorkerThreads
element.short: Maximum number of worker threads the pool may create

element.name: TThreadPool.MinWorkerThreads
element.short: Number of worker threads the pool keeps even when idle

element.name: TThreadPool.UnlimitedWorkerThreadsWhenBlocked
element.short: Declared for Delphi compatibility; it currently has no effect

descr.p: The property is declared with default True, but the pool neither initializes nor reads the field, so it reads False on a new pool and setting it changes nothing.

element.name: TThreadPool.Interactive
element.short: When True, waiting for this pool's tasks in the main thread keeps processing TThread.Synchronize and TThread.Queue requests

descr.p: With Interactive set, , and called from the main thread poll with CheckSynchronize instead of blocking on an event. This avoids a deadlock when a task calls TThread.Synchronize while the main thread waits for it.

element.name: TThreadPool.OnThreadStart
element.short: Called in each new worker thread when it registers with the pool

element.name: TThreadPool.OnThreadTerminate
element.short: Called in a worker thread just before it leaves the pool

descr.p: The handler runs in the terminating thread before the pool joins it. Do not call TThread.Synchronize from it if the pool may be destroyed from the main thread: waits for the thread, which in turn waits for the main thread.

element.name: TThreadPool.Default
element.short: Process-wide pool used when no pool is passed; created when the unit is initialized and freed at program finalization

element.name: TThreadPool.Current
element.short: Pool of the task running in the current thread, or outside a task

element.name: GetThreadPoolInteractive
element.short: Returns the setting of a pool

element.name: SetThreadPoolInteractive
element.short: Changes the setting of a pool

element.name: TTaskAwaitHook
element.short: Function type of : suspends the calling coroutine until a task has finished, or returns False if the caller is not a suspendable coroutine

element.name: TaskAwaitHook
element.short: Hook through which waits without timeout suspend a coroutine instead of blocking its thread; installed by fcl-coroutines

descr.p: and without a timeout, and therefore and the await operator, call the hook before blocking. When it returns True the task has finished and the wait completes without blocking the thread. The unit async.fiber installs a hook that suspends the current TFiber.

element.name: TaskOnComplete
element.short: Calls a procedure once a task has finished, without creating a continuation task

descr.p: The procedure runs in the thread that completes the task, or at once in the calling thread if the task is already finished. Unlike it never runs on the pool, is not affected by cancellation tokens and cannot be canceled. Keep it short: it delays the thread that completed the task.

element.name: TThreadPoolStats
element.short: Snapshot of a thread pool's counters, for monitoring and diagnostics

descr.p: The values are copied from the pool without locking, at the moment , or is called. They describe the pool's state approximately and must not be used for synchronization.

element.name: TThreadPoolStats.Get
element.short: Returns a snapshot of the given pool

element.name: TThreadPoolStats.Current
element.short: Snapshot of

element.name: TThreadPoolStats.Default
element.short: Snapshot of

element.short: Number of worker threads waiting for work

element.name: TThreadPoolStats.QueuedRequestCount
element.short: Number of queued work items that have not started yet

element.name: TThreadPoolStats.RetiredWorkerThreadCount
element.short: Number of worker threads that are retiring because they were idle

element.short: Average CPU usage in percent, as measured by the pool monitor

element.short: Most recent CPU usage sample in percent

element.short: Tick count (milliseconds) at which a worker thread was last suspended

element.name: TThreadPoolStats.LastQueuedRequestCount

element.name: TTaskStatus
element.short: Life-cycle state of a task, returned by

element.name: TTaskStatus.Created
element.short: Created but not started yet ()

element.name: TTaskStatus.WaitingToRun
element.short: Started and queued on the pool, waiting for a worker thread

element.name: TTaskStatus.Running
element.short: The task body is executing

element.name: TTaskStatus.Completed
element.short: Finished without an exception (terminal state)

element.name: TTaskStatus.WaitingForChildren
element.short: The body has finished but child tasks or loop replicas are still running

element.name: TTaskStatus.Canceled
element.short: Canceled before or while running (terminal state); waiting for the task raises EOperationCancelled

element.name: TTaskStatus.Exception
element.short: Finished with an unhandled exception (terminal state); waiting for the task raises

element.name: TTaskContinuationOption
element.short: Flags that control whether and how a continuation runs

descr.p: A continuation is attached with , , or . When the antecedent reaches a terminal status, the continuation is checked against all flags in the set; if any flag excludes that status, the continuation is not run and its own task becomes Canceled.

element.name: TTaskContinuationOption.NotOnCompleted
element.short: Do not run if the antecedent completed successfully

element.name: TTaskContinuationOption.NotOnFaulted
element.short: Do not run if the antecedent finished with an exception

element.name: TTaskContinuationOption.NotOnCanceled
element.short: Do not run if the antecedent was canceled; without an explicit token the continuation also uses the antecedent's token

element.name: TTaskContinuationOption.OnlyOnCompleted
element.short: Run only if the antecedent completed successfully

element.name: TTaskContinuationOption.OnlyOnFaulted
element.short: Run only if the antecedent finished with an exception

element.name: TTaskContinuationOption.OnlyOnCanceled
element.short: Run only if the antecedent was canceled

element.name: TTaskContinuationOption.ExecuteSynchronously
element.short: Run the continuation in the thread that completes the antecedent instead of queuing it on the pool

descr.p: If the antecedent has already finished when the continuation is attached, the continuation runs immediately in the calling thread. Use this only for short continuations: they delay the thread that completed the antecedent.

element.name: TTaskContinuationOptions
element.short: Set of flags; [] runs the continuation for any terminal status

element.name: TCancellationTokenRegistration
element.short: Handle of a callback registered with

descr.p: Call Unregister to remove the callback when it is no longer needed. A registration of , or of a token that was already canceled when the callback was registered, is empty; unregistering it does nothing.

element.name: TCancellationTokenRegistration.Unregister
element.short: Removes the callback; if the callback is running in another thread, waits until it returns

descr.p: After Unregister returns, the callback is not running and will not be called, so the data it uses can be freed. Calling Unregister from inside the callback itself does not wait. Calling it more than once is harmless.

element.name: TCancellationToken
element.short: Value type that tells tasks, futures, loops and asynchronous I/O whether cancellation was requested

descr.p: A token is obtained from , or for a token that is never canceled. It is a record holding a reference-counted pointer to the source's state: copying it is cheap, and a token remains valid after its source is freed (it then simply never becomes canceled).

Pass the same token to , , , , or the fcl-eventloop *Async methods to cancel a whole tree of operations at once. A task created while another task runs in the same thread inherits that task's token unless it receives its own.
Cancellation is cooperative: code that runs for a long time should check or call regularly.
All members are thread-safe.

element.name: TCancellationToken.None
element.short: Returns a token that is never canceled (CanBeCanceled = False)

element.name: TCancellationToken.CanBeCanceled
element.short: True if the token comes from a ; False for

element.name: TCancellationToken.IsCancellationRequested
element.short: True once the source has been canceled

descr.p: The check is a single memory read followed by a read barrier when it returns True; it makes no system call and can be used in tight loops.

element.name: TCancellationToken.WaitHandle
element.short: Manual-reset event that becomes signaled when the token is canceled; nil for

descr.p: The event is created on first access and is owned by the token's state: do not free it.

element.name: TCancellationToken.ThrowIfCancellationRequested
element.short: Raises EOperationCancelled if cancellation was requested

element.name: TCancellationToken.CheckCanceled
element.short: Same as

element.name: TCancellationToken.Register
element.short: Registers a callback to be called when the token is canceled

descr.p: The callback runs in the thread that calls (or in the timer thread of ). If the token is already canceled, the callback runs immediately in the calling thread and the returned registration is empty. For nothing is registered.
Callbacks must be short and must not raise exceptions: an exception stops the remaining callbacks and propagates to the code that called Cancel.

element.name: TCancellationToken.equal(TCancellationToken,TCancellationToken):Boolean
element.short: True if both tokens refer to the same cancellation state

element.name: TCancellationToken.notequal(TCancellationToken,TCancellationToken):Boolean
element.short: True if the tokens refer to different cancellation states

element.name: TCancellationTokenSource
element.short: Owner of a cancellation state: issues tokens and requests cancellation

descr.p: Call Cancel to cancel immediately, CancelAfter (or a timed constructor) to cancel after a delay, and CreateLinkedTokenSource to combine several tokens.
A pending delayed cancellation is served by a dedicated thread that lives until the delay expires, the source is canceled or freed. Avoid creating thousands of timed sources at the same time.
The source must be freed by its owner. Tokens obtained from it stay valid after it is freed, but can no longer become canceled.

element.name: TCancellationTokenSource.Create
element.short: Creates a source; the overloads with a delay call CancelAfter

element.name: TCancellationTokenSource.CreateLinkedTokenSource
element.short: Creates a new source that is canceled as soon as any of the given tokens is canceled

descr.p: Tokens that cannot be canceled are ignored. The caller owns the new source and must free it; freeing it removes its registrations from the input tokens. The new source can also be canceled directly.

element.name: TCancellationTokenSource.Cancel
element.short: Requests cancellation: sets the token, signals WaitHandle and runs the registered callbacks in the calling thread

descr.p: Only the first call has an effect; later calls return immediately.

element.name: TCancellationTokenSource.CancelAfter
element.short: Cancels the source after the given delay; a delay of 0 cancels immediately

descr.p: A new call replaces a pending delay. The call does nothing if the source is already canceled. A negative TTimeSpan is treated as 0.

element.name: TCancellationTokenSource.Reset
element.short: Replaces the cancellation state with a new, uncanceled one

descr.p: Tokens obtained before Reset keep referring to the old state; read Token again after resetting. Reset also stops a pending CancelAfter and removes the links of a source created by CreateLinkedTokenSource, so the source no longer follows its input tokens.

element.name: TCancellationTokenSource.Token
element.short: Token bound to the source's current cancellation state

element.name: TCancellationTokenSource.IsCancellationRequested
element.short: True once the source has been canceled

element.name: TCancellationTokenSource.WaitHandle
element.short: Manual-reset event signaled on cancellation; see

element.name: ITask
element.short: Interface of an asynchronous unit of work

descr.p: ITask gives control over a task's life cycle (, , ), its state () and non-blocking continuations (, ). Tasks are reference counted; a task that has been started keeps running even if the program drops its last reference.

element.name: ITask.Wait
element.short: Blocks until the task finishes or the timeout expires; returns False on timeout

descr.p: When the task has finished, Wait raises:

ul.li: EOperationCancelled if the task was canceled or its cancellation token has been canceled (also when the token is canceled after the task completed);

with all collected exceptions if the task or one of its child tasks raised an exception. The exceptions are handed over to the raised object, so a second Wait on the same task does not raise them again.

descr.p: Inside a coroutine (see ), Wait without a timeout suspends the coroutine instead of blocking. Elsewhere, calling Wait from a pool thread blocks that thread. Waiting in many tasks for other tasks of the same pool can use up all its workers; prefer or there. In the main thread of an Interactive pool, Wait keeps processing TThread.Synchronize requests.

element.name: ITask.Start
element.short: Queues a task in the Created state on its pool and returns it

descr.p: Starting an already started task does nothing. Starting a canceled task completes it as canceled without running it. Starting a task that has already finished raises EInvalidOperation. and return tasks that are already started.

element.name: ITask.Cancel
element.short: Cancels the task if it has not finished; a task that has not started yet will not run

descr.p: A running task is not interrupted: its body runs to the end unless it checks . Use a to cancel several tasks together.

element.name: ITask.CheckCanceled
element.short: Raises EOperationCancelled if the task was canceled or its token has been canceled

descr.p: Call it inside a long-running task body, typically as TTask.CurrentTask.CheckCanceled.

element.name: ITask.ContinueWith
element.short: Creates a task that runs aAction after this task finishes, without blocking a thread while waiting

descr.p: The continuation receives the antecedent task and runs on the pool when the antecedent reaches a terminal status (Completed, Canceled or Exception). Use to run it only for some of these, and ExecuteSynchronously to run it in the completing thread. If the options exclude the antecedent's status, or aCancelToken is canceled first, the continuation does not run and the returned task becomes Canceled.

The continuation runs on aPool, or on the antecedent's pool when aPool is nil. An exception in the antecedent is not raised in the continuation: inspect aAntecedent.Status or call aAntecedent.Wait to get it.

element.short: Current life-cycle state of the task

element.name: ITask.Id
element.short: Process-wide unique number of the task

element.short: Dynamic array of tasks

element.short: Procedure reference receiving a task; the action type of

element.short: Dynamic array of

element.short: Dynamic array of objects

element.name: IFuture
element.short: Task that produces a value of type T

descr.p: IFuture<T> extends with Value, which waits for the computation and returns its result, and with typed continuations (, , ).

The interface has no GUID, so it cannot be used with as or Supports. To get the future back from an ITask parameter (for example inside ThenBy), use a hard cast IFuture<T>(aTask), which is only valid if the task really is an IFuture<T>.

element.name: IFuture.StartFuture
element.short: Starts a future in the Created state and returns it; see

element.name: IFuture.Value
element.short: Waits for the computation to finish and returns its result

descr.p: Value calls without a timeout, so it raises the same exceptions: EOperationCancelled if the future was canceled and if the computation raised an exception. Reading Value inside a pool task blocks that worker thread.

element.name: IFuture.ContinueWith
element.short: Creates a task that runs aAction with this future after it finishes

descr.p: Works like , but the action receives the typed future, so it can read Value without a cast. Reading Value of a faulted or canceled future raises its exception in the continuation.

element.name: IFuture.Map
element.short: Returns a future that applies aFunc (T -> T) to this future's value

descr.p: Shorthand for ThenBy<T, T>. If this future is canceled or faults, aFunc is not called and the returned future takes over the cancellation or the exception.
aFunc is a , so its parameter must be declared const, also in an arrow function: F.Map((const X: Integer) => X * 2).

element.name: TITaskHelper
element.short: Type helper that adds the typed ThenBy continuations to ITask and IFuture<T>

element.name: TITaskHelper.ThenBy
element.short: Returns a future computed from the antecedent's result after the antecedent finishes, without blocking a thread while waiting

descr.p: There are three groups of overloads:

ul.li: ThenBy<T, TResult>(TFunc1<T, TResult>) passes the antecedent's value to the function. The antecedent must be an IFuture<T> of exactly this T; this is not checked. If the antecedent faults or is canceled, the function is not called and the result takes over the exception or the cancellation.
ThenBy<TResult>(TFunc1<ITask, TResult>) passes the antecedent task itself.
ThenBy<TResult>(TFunc<TResult>) runs a function without arguments.

descr.p: For the last two groups the antecedent's exception or cancellation is propagated only when aOptions is empty. With non-empty options the function runs whenever the options allow it, which can be used for recovery, for example ThenBy<string>(@Recover, [TTaskContinuationOption.OnlyOnFaulted]).

A propagated exception is moved from the antecedent to the returned future: waiting for the antecedent afterwards does not raise it again. Without an explicit token the continuation uses the antecedent's token; without an explicit pool, the antecedent's pool.
With {$modeswitch implicitgenerics} the type arguments can usually be inferred: Next := Fut.ThenBy(function(const Prev: ITask): Integer begin ... end);.

element.name: TTask
element.short: Factory for tasks and futures, and the class that implements ITask

descr.p: Use the class methods to create tasks (), to create and start them (, ), to chain typed continuations () and to wait for several tasks (, ). Work with the returned interfaces; do not create or free TTask objects directly.

element.name: TTask.Create
element.short: Creates a task in the Created state; call to queue it

descr.p: The class function overloads take a procedure reference or a TNotifyEvent with its sender, and optionally a cancellation token and a pool (default: ). The parameterless constructor exists only to prevent direct construction and raises ENoConstructException.

element.name: TTask.CurrentTask
element.short: Task executing in the current thread, or nil outside a task

descr.p: Inside the body of it returns the loop replica that runs the iteration.

element.name: TTask.Run
element.short: Creates a task, starts it and returns it

descr.p: Equivalent to TTask.Create(...).Start. With a aCancelToken the task is canceled when the token is canceled; if it has not started yet it will not run.

element.name: TTask.Future
element.short: Starts a function on the pool and returns an IFuture<T> for its result

descr.p: With {$modeswitch implicitgenerics}, T can be inferred from the function: F := TTask.Future(function: Integer begin Result := 42; end);. With an arrow function the result type is that of the expression, so TTask.Future(() => 1) is an IFuture<ShortInt>; write (): Integer => 1 when another type is needed.

element.name: TTask.ThenBy
element.short: Class-method form of that takes the antecedent task as the first argument

element.name: TTask.WaitForAll
element.short: Waits until all tasks have finished; returns False on timeout

descr.p: When all tasks have finished, WaitForAll raises with the exceptions of all faulted tasks, or EOperationCancelled if no task faulted but at least one was canceled. An empty array returns True immediately. Without a timeout, tasks that are still queued may be executed in the calling thread.

element.name: TTask.WaitForAny
element.short: Waits until at least one task has finished and returns its index, or -1 on timeout

descr.p: If the first finished task was canceled or faulted, WaitForAny raises its exception (EOperationCancelled or ) instead of returning the index. An empty array returns -1.

descr.p: TParallel distributes loop iterations () or a list of procedures () over a , using up to 2 * ProcessorCount self-replicating tasks.

element.name: TParallel.For
element.short: Runs the iterations of the inclusive range [aLowInclusive..aHighInclusive] in parallel and waits until they are done

descr.p: For blocks the calling thread until the loop is finished, then returns a . Iterations run in no particular order. In a loop that completes normally each iteration runs exactly once. An empty range (aHighInclusive < aLowInclusive) returns Completed = True without running anything.
The overloads differ in:

ul.li: the index type: Integer or Int64;
the body: a procedure reference or a method with aSender, with or without a parameter. Only the bodies with loop state can call Break or Stop;
aStride: the number of consecutive iterations a worker takes at a time at the start. The stride grows while the loop runs; increase it for very cheap iterations;
aCancelToken: when it is canceled, workers stop taking new iterations and For returns Completed = False without raising an exception. A loop inside a task uses that task's token when it gets none;

descr.p: If iterations raise exceptions, the loop stops starting new iterations and For raises an with all collected exceptions in the calling thread.
Because For is a reserved word, call it as TParallel.&For(...).

element.name: TParallel.Join
element.short: Starts a task that runs several procedures or TNotifyEvent handlers in parallel, and returns it

descr.p: Join does not wait: call Wait on the returned to wait for all procedures. Exceptions raised by the procedures are re-raised by Wait in an . With aCancelToken, procedures that have not started when the token is canceled are skipped.

element.name: TParallel.TLoopState
element.short: Loop control object passed to the bodies of TParallel.For that take a loop state

descr.p: Each worker replica has its own instance; do not keep it after the body returns.

ul.li: Break stops the loop after the current iteration, but all iterations with a lower index still run. Use it for an ordered search for the first match.
Stop stops the loop as soon as possible, with no guarantee about other iterations. Use it for an unordered search for any match.
ShouldExit tells a long iteration that it can give up.

element.name: TParallel.TLoopState.Break
element.short: Ends the loop after the iterations below the current index; the lowest such index is reported in

element.name: TParallel.TLoopState.Stop
element.short: Ends the loop as soon as possible; iterations that have not started will not run

element.name: TParallel.TLoopState.ShouldExit
element.short: True if the current iteration does not need to finish: the loop was stopped, canceled or faulted, or Break was called at a lower index

element.name: TParallel.TLoopState.Faulted
element.short: True if an iteration has raised an exception

element.name: TParallel.TLoopState.Stopped
element.short: True if an iteration has called Stop

element.name: TParallel.TLoopState.Cancelled
element.short: True if the loop's cancellation token has been canceled

element.name: TParallel.TLoopState.LowestBreakIteration
element.short: Lowest index at which Break has been called so far, or Null
